When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Cloudflare (NET).

Cloudflare currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.88, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 32 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.88 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 32 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 20 are Strong Buy and two are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 62.5% and 6.3% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for NET
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for NET

Check price target & stock forecast for Cloudflare here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Cloudflare, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

What Happened?

Zscaler (ZS) closed at $255.15 on October 23, up 7.31% on the day and 23% across five straight gains from $207.38 on October 16. Peers moved with it that Friday: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) rose 7.22%, CrowdStrike (CRWD) 8.25% and Cloudflare (NET) 7.29%, as an Evercore ISI survey of security resellers pointed to firmer budgets and the PHP patching scramble continued. The run has lifted Zscaler above Wall Street's mean target, which leaves a narrower question: what is left for a buyer at $255?

Zscaler Drawdowns (TIKR)
Chaudhry's Warning Was About Speed

The biggest gain came on October 21, when Zscaler rose 7.84% as security stocks rallied on critical flaws in PHP, the language behind roughly 70% of websites, which researchers found with AI's help, according to The New Stack. That beat Okta (OKTA) at 7.54%, Cloudflare at 5.32% and CrowdStrike at 5.26%.

At its October 6 Investor Day, CEO Jay Chaudhry framed the risk as one of speed: frontier models find flaws, and "the gap between discovery to exploitation, which used to be months is now becoming minutes or seconds." He said Zscaler has run more than 400 assessments with large Global 2000 customers since the preview program for Mythos, Anthropic's frontier model. One energy customer had about 6,614 internet-facing assets, 1,049 software vulnerabilities and 40 VPN appliances.

Chief Product Officer Adam Geller summed up the answer: "If you are reachable, you're breachable." Zscaler hides applications behind its exchange, and its Autonomous AppShield adds virtual patches before customers have a chance to patch. Geller said the most common request after those assessments is what to do next, and Zscaler points customers to its private access product, ZPA. Chaudhry discussed the PHP flaws on Fox Business after the disclosure.

The pitch has a clear boundary. Chaudhry said Zscaler hides applications that require authentication. Public websites have to stay reachable, so not every PHP fix becomes new Zscaler business.

Zscaler (ZS) stock has returned 73.2% over the past three months, compared with 3.1% for the S&P 500. That bounce follows a long slide, and shares remain 24.1% below their highest close of the past year, set in November 2025. Buying at $255.15 means betting that Zscaler's growth holds up. So, have you already missed the cheap price in Zscaler?

What Are You Paying For Zscaler Stock Now?

The cheapest price of recent years has passed. At the latest close, Zscaler traded at 12.3 times its sales over the past twelve months. At the end of June 2026, those same sales were priced at 6.8 times, the lowest multiple at any of the last 34 quarter ends.

Because Zscaler still reports a loss, a price-to-earnings ratio means nothing here. Over the four quarters to July 2026, the company posted an operating loss of 3.6% of revenue, though that was the smallest loss at any of 35 quarter ends since fiscal 2018. The business runs on cash instead: Zscaler generated $1.13 billion in operating cash over those twelve months, and the stock trades at 36.6 times that cash flow, compared with 15.3 times for the S&P 500.

Behind that cash generation is a subscription base that is still growing fast. On the September 3 call, management said annual recurring revenue reached $3.8 billion in fiscal Q4 2026, up 25% from a year earlier. They added that growth in newly added recurring revenue, excluding Red Canary, picked up from 7% in fiscal 2025 to 17% in fiscal Q4 2026.

What Must Zscaler Deliver In Fiscal Q1 2027?

The bar for Zscaler is management's own guidance. Management guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $935 million to $939 million and reaffirmed that range at its Investor Day on October 6.

For the full year, management has guided to slower growth, forecasting revenue to rise 16.6% to 17.5% in fiscal 2027, compared with 25.4% in fiscal 2026. Part of the growth in fiscal 2026 came from Red Canary, a business Zscaler acquired, which added $144 million of revenue. Excluding Red Canary, revenue grew 20%.

Management said AI is driving demand for its Zero Trust platform and data security. The company has not called out the contribution from security for AI in its guidance.

Zscaler Stock Has Mostly Fallen After Its Reports

Over the company's last six reports, shares fell in the two trading days following five of them. The deepest decline was a 29.6% drop after the May 2026 report, while the sole gain was a 16.8% rise following the May 2025 report.

What happened?

A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after cybersecurity stocks surged as investors reacted to a massive new wave of artificial intelligence-enabled cyber threats that industry experts have dubbed "Black October."

As reported by CNBC, U.S. security agencies including the National Security Agency and FBI issued urgent warnings regarding critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the core programming language used to build nearly 70% of the internet. Cybersecurity teams globally are now in a frantic scramble to patch these security flaws, which were discovered utilizing advanced AI models, CNBC explained. CNBC noted that the extreme urgency of the situation was underscored by industry executives who stated that the last two days alone have seen dozens of cyberattacks that individually would normally represent the worst breach of an entire calendar year. In response to these unprecedented threats, federal agencies have recommended that organizations make immediate fixes to their code or take vulnerable legacy systems completely offline, according to CNBC.

Consequently, CNBC reported that Wall Street analysts view this rapidly evolving threat landscape as a massive long-term catalyst for the sector, with experts highlighting that cybersecurity platform providers will be the clear beneficiaries of continued AI development. As a result, shares across the identity management and network security space rallied sharply as organizations rushed to upgrade their defensive postures against these AI-driven exploits, CNBC concluded.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

The P/S lens fits Cloudflare because sales, not earnings, are the cleaner anchor for a business still reinvesting heavily. On this yardstick, the stock trades on a P/S of 43.0x, which is far above both the IT sector average of 2.0x and the 13.8x peer group level for similar infrastructure and security players. A tailored Fair Ratio that blends Cloudflare's growth profile, margin structure, size and risk highlights this as a rich valuation, with the current multiple sitting meaningfully above that benchmark. The PHP2Shell response and the positive reaction it triggered help explain why investors are willing to ascribe such a premium to Cloudflare's security and AI traffic franchise. Even so, the gap to sector and peer norms still leaves little room for missteps on execution or demand. Cloudflare Soars 6% as PHP Flaw Hitting 70% of Websites Lifts Security Stocks ©maxkabakov from Getty Images, Yuri_Arcurs from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock rose 6% and Datadog rose 7% today after PHP patched two critical flaws in software that runs an estimated 70% of websites.

Cloudflare gave every customer firewall rules against the known attacks, including free users, which shows why its place in front of millions of sites is valuable.

Analysts expect Cloudflare's revenue to more than double, from $2.17 billion in 2025 to $4.73 billion in 2028.

The stock was already richly valued after a big run this year, so watch whether CISA lists the flaw and whether free users move to paid plans.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock jumped 6% today after PHP rushed out emergency patches for two critical flaws in the software behind an estimated 70% of the world's websites. Other stocks tied to protecting websites and apps rose too, including Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ), up 7%.

What exactly happened

The flaws let an attacker take over any web server running PHP 5.4 or later. One of them can also leak passwords, session tokens and API keys. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont called it "one of the biggest vulns in years."

Attackers didn't wait for the fix. Cloudflare logged the first attacks at 3:43 a.m. ET, hours before the official patch landed around 10 a.m. ET.

Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht's response:

"PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free."

TIKR tracks 34 analysts on Cloudflare. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Cloudflare, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Cloudflare's Analyst Ratings

The free tier earns its keep

That last line is the story. Cloudflare sits in front of millions of PHP sites, so one set of rules covered all of them at once, before most of their owners could patch.

That's why it pays to give protection away. Every free site Cloudflare shields in a crisis like this one gives its owner a reason to stay, and eventually to pay.

And the paid business is growing fast. Analysts expect revenue to more than double, from $2.17 billion in 2025 to $4.73 billion in 2028…

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

Nothing in today's news should move those estimates yet. That would take site owners signing up for paid plans after the scare, and the next few quarters will show whether they do.

A big day at a steep price

Today's pop comes right after Cloudflare dropped 15% in a week. Before that, a run had the stock up 78% since January by early October. Before today's move it already traded at nearly 200x forward earnings, and today's jump pushes that higher.
